21956-report-of-the-knaresbrough-rail-wa.creator: Unknown
21956-report-of-the-knaresbrough-rail-wa.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. At a meeting held the 16th day of March, 1818, in the Town's-Hall, at Knaresbro', your Committee were authorised to appoint a suitable person to take a survey of the country, in order to point out the most eligible line for a Canal to Knaresbro'.

arxiv-2212-03696.title: Non-linear fluctuating hydrodynamics for KPZ scaling in isotropic spin chains
arxiv-2212-03696.creator: Jacopo De Nardis, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Romain Vasseur
arxiv-2212-03696.description: Abstract Finite temperature spin transport in integrable isotropic spin chains is known to be superdiffusive, with dynamical spin correlations that are conjectured to fall into the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) universality class. However, integrable spin chains have time-reversal and parity symmetries that are absent from the KPZ/stochastic Burgers equation, which force higher-order spin fluctuations to deviate from standard KPZ predictions.

arxiv-2310-03048.title: DRAGONS - A Quick Overview Journal: RNAAS Facilities: Gemini:South, Gemini:Gillett DRAGONS DOI:10.5281/zenodo.4025470, Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 )

arxiv-2310-03048.description: Abstract DRAGONS (Data Reduction for Astronomy from Gemini Observatory North and South) is a platform for the reduction and processing of astronomical data. The Python-based, open-source package includes infrastructure for automation and algorithms for the processing of imaging and spectroscopic data, up to the analysis-ready stage.

arxiv-2405-01807.title: Algorithmic Decision-Making under Agents with Persistent Improvement
arxiv-2405-01807.creator: Tian Xie, Xuwei Tan, Xueru Zhang
arxiv-2405-01807.description: Abstract This paper studies algorithmic decision-making under human strategic behavior, where a decision maker uses an algorithm to make decisions about human agents, and the latter with information about the algorithm may exert effort strategically and improve to receive favorable decisions.

arxiv-2408-13984.title: Non-invertible flavor symmetries in magnetized extra dimensions
arxiv-2408-13984.creator: Tatsuo Kobayashi 1 and, Hajime Otsuka 2
arxiv-2408-13984.description: Abstract We discuss non-invertible symmetries in toroidal compactifications of higher dimensional Yang-Mills theory with magnetic fluxes, which can be regarded as an effective action of type IIB string theory with magnetized D-branes. Specifically, we derive fusion rules of discrete isometry operators, which are invariant under the ℤ N \mathbb{Z}_{N} orbifold twist.

arxiv-2408-17001.creator: Marc Kaufmann, Bogdan Popa
arxiv-2408-17001.description: Abstract . Surveys and experiments in economics involve stateful interactions: participants receive different messages based on earlier answers, choices, and performance, or trade across many rounds with other participants. In the design of Congame, a platform for running such economic studies, we decided to use delimited continuations to manage the common flow of participants through a study.

arxiv-2506-06952.title: La T t E - F l o w : Layerwise Timestep-Expert Flow-based Transformer
arxiv-2506-06952.creator: Ying Shen, Zhiyang Xu, Jiuhai Chen, Shizhe Diao, Jiaxin Zhang, Yuguang Yao Joy Rimchala Ismini Lourentzou Lifu Huang
arxiv-2506-06952.description: Abstract Recent advances in multimodal foundation models unifying image understanding and generation have opened exciting avenues for tackling a wide range of vision-language tasks within a single framework. Despite progress, existing unified models typically require extensive pretraining and struggle to achieve the same level of performance compared to models dedicated to each task.

arxiv-2507-17524.title: SDC-Net: A Domain Adaptation Framework with Semantic-Dynamic Consistency for Cross-Subject EEG Emotion Recognition
arxiv-2507-17524.creator: Jiahao Tang, Youjun Li, Xiangting Fan, Yangxuan Zheng, Siyuan Lu, Xueping Li, Peng Fang, Chenxi Li, Zi-Gang Huang
arxiv-2507-17524.description: Abstract Electroencephalography(EEG) based emotion recognition holds great promise for affective brain-computer interfaces (aBCIs), yet practical deployment remains challenging due to substantial inter-subject variability and the lack of labeled data in target domains. To overcome these limitations, we present a novel unsupervised Semantic-Dynamic Consistency domain adaptation network for fully label-free cross-subject EEG emotion recognition.

pmc-10571828.title: The Effects of Different Types of Sleep Disorder on Colorectal Cancer: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study
pmc-10571828.creator: Po-Lin Chiang, Wen-Rui Hao, Hong-Jye Hong, Chun-Chao Chen, Chun-Chih Chiu, Yu-Ann Fang, Tsung-Lin Yang, Yu-Hsin Lai, Ming-Yao Chen, Min-Huei Hsu, Kuan-Rau Chiou, Kuan-Jie Lin, Tsung-Yeh Yang, Hsin Hsiu, Ju-Chi Liu, Luca Roncucci
pmc-10571828.description: Simple SummaryIn this study, we used Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database to investigate the potential association between sleep disorder (SD) and colorectal cancer (CRC) after matching 177,707 patients with SD and without a history of CRC with 177,707 non-SD and non-CRC Taiwanese citizens without SD and without CRC based on age and gender.

pmc-10615540.title: Assessment of extremity dose for medical staff involved in positron emission tomography/computed tomography imaging: Retrospective study
pmc-10615540.creator: Rabiye Uslu Erdemir, Mohamed Mahmoud Abuzaid, Baris Cavli, Huseyin Ozan Tekin, Wiam Elshami
pmc-10615540.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). There has been an increase in positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) imaging procedures, and medical workers involved in PET/CT are at increased risk of occupational exposure. Data on extremity dose exposure are limited globally. The current study aimed to evaluate the occupational radiation dose for extremities for medical workers (nurses, radiographers/radiologic technologists, and nuclear medicine physicians) working in PET/CT scanners at 5 large hospitals in Turkey.

pmc-11290102.title: Genetic variation at a splicing branch point in intron 7 of STK11: a rare variant decreasing its expression in a Chinese family with Peutz–Jeghers syndrome
pmc-11290102.creator: Xiufang Wang, Yuanyuan Li, Jingqiong Zhang, Chao Liu, Aiping Deng, Juyi Li
pmc-11290102.description: BackgroundPeutz–Jeghers syndrome (PJS), a rare dominantly inherited disease, is primarily characterized by hamartomatous polyps and melanotic macules as well as by an increased risk of cancer. The current study aimed to identify the pathogenic gene and pathogenic mechanism of a proband with PJS, thereby offering precise prevention and treatment strategies for PJS.

pmc-11514958.title: Ceftazidime-avibactam resistance in KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae accompanied hypermucoviscosity acquisition
pmc-11514958.creator: Yingyi Guo, Jiong Wang, Likang Yao, Yijing Wang, Yan Zhang, Chuyue Zhuo, Xu Yang, Feifeng Li, Jiahui Li, Baomo Liu, Nanhao He, Jiakang Chen, Shunian Xiao, Zhiwei Lin, Chao Zhuo
pmc-11514958.description: BackgroundAntimicrobial resistance and bacterial hypermucoviscosity, associated with escalating production of capsules, constitute major challenges for the clinical management of Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) infections. This study investigates the association and underlying mechanism between ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) resistance and bacterial hypermucoviscosity in Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC)-producing K. pneumoniae (KPC-Kp).

pmc-11656258.title: Water-Induced Turn-on of Lanthanide Photoluminescence Emission and Application in Colorimetric Sensing of Trace Water
pmc-11656258.creator: Malee Sinchow, Rania Chaicharoen, Thammanoon Chuasaard, Bunlawee Yotnoi, Chalermpong Saenjum, Athipong Ngamjarurojana, Apinpus Rujiwatra
pmc-11656258.description: To examine the water-induced photoluminescence turn-on and its potential application in trace water sensing, a new series of [LnIII(dmba)3(H2O)2]·2H2O, where LnIII = LaIII (I), PrIII (II), NdIII (III), SmIII (IV), EuIII (V), GdIII (VI), TbIII (VII), DyIII (VIII), HoIII (IX), and ErIII (X), were synthesized using dimethoxybenzoic acid (Hdmba).

pmc-11677035.title: Peptide-Purified Anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate Receptor (NMDAR) Autoantibodies Have Inhibitory Effect on Long-Term Synaptic Plasticity
pmc-11677035.creator: Charlotte Day, John-Paul Silva, Rebecca Munro, Brice Mullier, Véronique Marie André, Christian Wolff, Gary J Stephens, Angela Bithell, Giuseppe Biagini
pmc-11677035.description: Background/Objectives: Recent studies, typically using patient cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), have suggested that different autoantibodies (Aabs) acting on their respective receptors, may underlie neuropsychiatric disorders. The GluN1 (NR1) subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) has been identified as a target of anti-NMDAR Aabs in a number of central nervous system (CNS) diseases, including encephalitis and autoimmune epilepsy.

pmc-11678908.title: Diet and Microbiota Modulation for Chronic Pouchitis: Evidence, Challenges, and Opportunities
pmc-11678908.creator: Pierluigi Puca, Angelo Del Gaudio, Guia Becherucci, Franco Sacchetti, Luigi Sofo, Loris Riccardo Lopetuso, Alfredo Papa, Giovanni Cammarota, Franco Scaldaferri
pmc-11678908.description: Chronic pouchitis occurs in about 50% of patients undergoing a restorative proctocolectomy for ulcerative colitis. This affection represents a significant therapeutic challenge, particularly for symptomatic patients who do not respond to antibiotic treatments and biologic therapies. Several dietary approaches, including low FODMAP diets and the Mediterranean diet, have shown promising results in improving symptoms and disease burden.

pmc-12615379.title: A novel method for detecting brown planthopper (Nilaparvata lugens Stål) early infestation using dual-temporal hyperspectral images
pmc-12615379.creator: Xuying Huang, Shun Jiang, Shanshan Feng, Lei Zhang, Yangying Gan, Lianlian Hou, Chengrui Mao, Ruiqing Chen, Hanxiang Xiao, Yanfang Li, Zhanghua Xu, Canfang Zhou
pmc-12615379.description: Accurate and prompt monitoring of brown planthopper (BPH) infestation is crucial for rice production stability. The unique advantages of remote sensing in mapping the location and severity of pest damage are widely acknowledged. However, the crypticity of BPH early damage complicates the identification of infested areas.

pmc-12629013.title: Staphylococcus aureus nasal carriage is associated with faster symptom resolution following nasal allergen challenge in ragweed-allergic participants: a subset of the Allergic Rhinitis Microbiome Study
pmc-12629013.creator: Sophia Linton, Lubnaa Hossenbaccus, Abigail Davis, Jenny Thiele, Sarah Garvey, Hannah Botting, Lisa Steacy, Prameet M. Sheth, Anne K. Ellis
pmc-12629013.description: In this letter, we report that ragweed-allergic participants with nasal Staphylococcus aureus carriage (n = 7) exhibited significantly smaller reductions in Peak Nasal Inspiratory Flow from baseline at 3 h (P = 0.013) and 5 h (P = 0.008) post–nasal allergen challenge compared to non-carriers (n = 12).

pmc-12672026.title: Major systemic infection following breast cancer surgery and oncological outcomes
pmc-12672026.creator: Linda Adwall, Irma Fredriksson, Hella Hultin, Peter Stålberg, Maria Mani, Olov Norlén, Helena Sackey
pmc-12672026.description: BackgroundPostoperative infections are well-known complications following cancer surgery and are associated with worse oncological outcomes in several cancer types. The influence of major systemic postoperative infections on the risk of breast cancer recurrence remains unexplored. The primary aim of this study was to assess the risk of distant recurrence following major systemic infection.

pmc-13155883.title: Syndrome catastrophique des antiphospholipides chez une femme de 39 ans
pmc-13155883.creator: Ayman Salih, Nezam Altorok, Ragheb Assaly, Fadi Safi
pmc-13155883.description: L) est une variante potentiellement mortelle du syndrome des antiphospholipides (SAPL) qui se caractérise par des thromboses multiples et évoluant rapidement, touchant au moins 3 systèmes organiques en l’espace de 1 semaine. Cette affection nécessite une reconnaissance rapide et une action multidisciplinaire, car des thromboses fulminantes touchant plusieurs systèmes organiques peuvent donner lieu à une maladie grave et mortelle.

pmc-13350631.title: Ultrasound assessment of blood flow in branches of the external carotid artery as potential donors for microsurgical revascularisation of the central nervous system
pmc-13350631.creator: Lukasz Dorobisz, Marcin Magdziarz, Dariusz Szarek
pmc-13350631.description: BackgroundVascular bypasses that connect branches of the superficial temporal artery (STA) to cerebral arteries are a recognised treatment option for carefully selected cases involving various cerebral vascular conditions. Among the different microsurgical techniques, one common method is the direct STA-middle cerebral artery (MCA) bypass.

pmc-13433981.title: Interpreting the clinical utility and generalizability of a multitask perioperative prediction model

This Matters Arising comments on Yoon et al.’s multitask gradient boosting model for predicting acute kidney injury, postoperative respiratory failure and in-hospital mortality after non-cardiac surgery. pmc-13577605.title: Testicular vascularization in healthy dogs using a microvascular flow imaging technique - MicroV
pmc-13577605.creator: Luisa Bittencourt de Lima Yamamoto, Diego Rodrigues Gomes, Luiz Paulo Nogueira Aires, Anna Carolina Mazeto Ercolin, Fredderico Garcia, Camila Silveira Stanquini, Desirée Rodrigues da Silva Alves, Andrea Degiovanni, Sâmara Turbay Pires, Javier Enrique Jerez Arevalo, Fernando Sebastiãn Baldi Rey, Marc
pmc-13577605.description: Testicular health significantly impacts the overall health and reproductive capacity of dogs, making early diagnosis of testicular conditions crucial. Neoplasms, orchitis, degeneration of the seminiferous epithelium, cryptorchidism, and testicular atrophy are among the most common testicular diseases in dogs. Ultrasonography is essential in andrological examinations, as it is a safe, easy-to-perform, and minimally invasive method.
